title: Zach Bryan Releases New EP and Announces 2027 Stadium Tour
text:
Zach Bryan releases his eight-song EP on Oct. 16 via Warner Records, featuring collaborations with Lana Del Rey and Turnpike Troubadours, and announces a 2027 stadium tour.
Zach Bryan has released a new eight-song EP on Friday, Oct. 16 via Warner Records. The collection includes collaborations with Lana Del Rey on the track Lies and Turnpike Troubadours on Plainsman. Other tracks on the EP include Robot Killed The Working Man and Backwards.
In January, Bryan released a 25-song album that debuted atop the all-genre Billboard 200 chart. He also soon after released an acoustic version of the album. The album included the song Plastic Cigarette, which rose to No. 13 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 2 on the Hot Country Songs chart.
2027 Stadium Tour Details Announced
Bryan has announced his upcoming stadium tour, the 2027 Young Manhood And Other Donatable Organs Tour, which will play 19 stadiums across North America and Australia next year.
The tour will feature support from John Fogerty, Ryan Bingham and The Texas Gentlemen, Vance Joy, Fey Fili, Gabriella Rose and Emma Ogier. Tickets for the tour go on sale to the public Friday, Oct. 23 at 10 a.m. local time at zachbryan.com.
The trek launches in North America on April 28 at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. It will include stops at Chicago’s Soldier Field, Atlanta’s Mercedes-Benz Stadium and Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field, before heading to Australia with performances at Melbourne’s Marvel Stadium, Sydney’s Accor Stadium and Brisbane’s Suncorp Stadium.
Chart Success and Previous Releases
Bryan earned a Hot 100 chart-topper in 2023 with the Kacey Musgraves collaboration I Remember Everything. In addition to his chart success, Bryan has built a reputation for his prolific output and captivating live performances.
The new EP marks another chapter in Bryan’s career, following the success of his previous album. With the upcoming stadium tour, Bryan is set to bring his music to even larger audiences across two continents.
